Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

An insured person is a person covered under an insurance policy, and the term encompasses several categories of individuals depending on the context of the policy. Generally, an insured person includes the person or persons shown as insured on the Policy Declarations (including under Coverage CW), relatives residing in the insured's household, and any other person in, on, getting into, or getting out of an insured auto with permission. Any other person or organization liable for the use of an insured auto is also considered an insured person if the use is by an insured person as described above. Additionally, the spouse of an insured person must be a resident of the same household at the time of an accident to qualify under that status.

An insured person is protected from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance, or use, including loading or unloading, of an insured auto. The insured person may be legally obligated to pay damages because of bodily injury and property damage, including bodily injury sustained by any person and damage to or destruction of property. An insured person may also be someone who incurs reasonable expenses for necessary medical treatment, services, or products, or who sustains continuous total disability as a direct result of bodily injury, sickness, or disease caused by an auto accident. An insured person may die as the result of a covered auto accident, and benefits are paid only while the insured person is alive. The insured person is the person to whom any amount due is payable.

Allstate defends an insured person when sued for damages covered by the policy, even if the suit is groundless or false. However, an insured person sued for damages not covered by the policy will not be defended by Allstate. The insured person may be asked to attend hearings or trials to defend against a bodily injury suit and may receive up to $50 per day for loss of wages or salary. The insured person must be informed immediately if sued as the result of an auto accident. The insured person must cooperate with the insurer in the investigation, settlement, and defense of any claim or lawsuit, and must help obtain payment from anyone jointly responsible. If an insured person sues a person believed responsible for the accident without giving the insurer notice, the insurer is not bound by any resulting judgment. The insured person may be required to take proper action to preserve all rights to recover damages. The insured person will be repaid by Allstate for interest accruing on damages awarded.

Allstate will pay for direct and accidental loss to your insured auto or a non-owned auto (including insured loss to an attached trailer) from a collision with another object or by upset of that auto or trailer. ## COVERAGE DE Diminishing Deductible Auto Collision Insurance

If the loss is $100 or more, Allstate will pay for direct and accidental loss to your insured auto or a non-owned auto (including insured loss to an attached trailer) from a collision with another object or by upset of that auto or trailer. No deductible applies to losses in excess of $100.

If the loss is between $50 and $100, you pay the difference between the amount of loss and $100. We will pay the rest of the loss up to our limits of liability.

If the loss is $50 or less, we will not make any payment.

If you have collision or comprehensive coverage under this policy and the loss involves either coverage, Allstate will repay you for your cost of renting an auto from a rental agency or garage. If your insured auto is disabled by a collision or comprehensive loss, coverage starts the day after the loss. If it is driveable, coverage starts the day after the auto is taken to the garage for repairs.

1. if the auto is disabled by a collision or comprehensive loss, completion of repairs or replacement of the auto;

However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. You agree to cooperate with us in determining if this information is correct, if it is complete, and if it changes during the policy period. You agree that if this information changes or is incorrect or incomplete, we may adjust your premium accordingly during the policy period.

Changes which result in a premium adjustment are contained in our rules. These include, but are not limited to:

1. autos insured by the policy, including changes in use.
2. drivers residing in your household, their ages or marital status.
3. coverages or coverage limits.
4. rating territory.
5. discount eligibility.

Any calculation or adjustment of your premium will be made using the rules, rates and forms in effect, and on file if required, for our use in your state.

When Allstate broadens a coverage during the policy period without additional charge, you have the new feature if you have the coverage to which it applies. 21,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

49,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

## Premium Changes

The premium for each auto is based on information Allstate has received from you or other sources. You agree to cooperate with us in determining if this information is correct, if it is complete, and if it changes during the policy period. You agree that if this information changes or is incorrect or incomplete, we may adjust your premium accordingly during the policy period.

Changes which result in a premium adjustment are contained in our rules. These include, but are not limited to:

1. autos insured by the policy, including changes in use.
2. drivers residing in your household, their ages or marital status.
3. coverages or coverage limits.
4. rating territory.
5. discount eligibility.

Any calculation or adjustment of your premium will be made using the rules, rates and forms in effect, and on file if required, for our use in your state.

## Coverage Changes

When Allstate broadens a coverage during the policy period without additional charge, you have the new feature if you have the coverage to which it applies. The new feature applies on the date the coverage change is effective in your state. Otherwise, the policy can be changed only by endorsement. Any change in your coverage will be made using the rules, rates and forms in effect, and on file if required, for our use in your state.

41,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

Under this policy, an insured person is protected from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto, and Allstate will defend an insured person sued for damages covered by the policy, even if the suit is groundless or false. The limits available for any other auto covered by the policy will not be added to the coverage for the involved or chosen auto.

The policy cannot be transferred to anyone without Allstate's written consent, and it can be changed only by endorsement. The insured may cancel the policy by writing to Allstate with the future date on which coverage should stop; a refund, if due, will be proportional to the time the policy has been in effect, but cancellation will be effective even if the refund is not made immediately. Allstate may cancel part or all of the policy by mailing notice to the insured at their last known address. During the first 60 days the original policy is in effect, Allstate will give at least 10 days' notice of cancellation. After the first 60 days, if Allstate cancels for any reason other than non-payment of premium, it will give 30 days' notice of cancellation. After the original policy has been in effect 60 days, Allstate will not cancel the policy unless certain conditions are met, namely: the premium is not paid when due; the insured or any member of their household is convicted of a crime due to acts which increase the hazard insured against; fraud or material misrepresentation is used in obtaining the policy or making a claim; an act or omission, or a violation of any condition of the policy, occurs during the policy period which substantially and materially increases the hazard insured against; a material change in the nature or extent of the risk occurs during the policy period which causes the risk of loss to be substantially and materially increased; or Allstate has mailed notice within the first 60 days that it does not intend to continue the policy. If Allstate does not intend to continue the policy beyond the current policy period, it will mail notice at least 30 days before the end of the policy period. Changes that result in a premium adjustment include, but are not limited to, autos insured by the policy, including changes in use.

An insured person is a person covered under an insurance policy, and the term encompasses several categories of individuals depending on the context of the policy. Generally, an insured person includes the person or persons shown as insured on the Policy Declarations (including under Coverage CW), relatives residing in the insured's household, and any other person in, on, getting into, or getting out of an insured auto with permission. Any other person or organization liable for the use of an insured auto is also considered an insured person if the use is by an insured person as described above. Additionally, the spouse of an insured person must be a resident of the same household at the time of an accident to qualify under that status.

An insured person is protected from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance, or use, including loading or unloading, of an insured auto. The insured person may be legally obligated to pay damages because of bodily injury and property damage, including bodily injury sustained by any person and damage to or destruction of property. An insured person may also be someone who incurs reasonable expenses for necessary medical treatment, services, or products, or who sustains continuous total disability as a direct result of bodily injury, sickness, or disease caused by an auto accident. An insured person may die as the result of a covered auto accident, and benefits are paid only while the insured person is alive. The insured person is the person to whom any amount due is payable.

Allstate defends an insured person when sued for damages covered by the policy, even if the suit is groundless or false. However, an insured person sued for damages not covered by the policy will not be defended by Allstate. The insured person may be asked to attend hearings or trials to defend against a bodily injury suit and may receive up to $50 per day for loss of wages or salary. The insured person must be informed immediately if sued as the result of an auto accident. The insured person must cooperate with the insurer in the investigation, settlement, and defense of any claim or lawsuit, and must help obtain payment from anyone jointly responsible. If an insured person sues a person believed responsible for the accident without giving the insurer notice, the insurer is not bound by any resulting judgment. The insured person may be required to take proper action to preserve all rights to recover damages. The insured person will be repaid by Allstate for interest accruing on damages awarded.

23,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

10,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

24,	"POLICY","DOCUMENT",The entity referred to as "POLICY" constitutes a legal insurance contract between the insured individual and the insurer, Allstate, that applies only during the policy period and may apply to an accident on a primary basis. Under this policy, an insured person is protected from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto, and Allstate will defend an insured person sued for damages covered by the policy, even if the suit is groundless or false. The limits available for any other auto covered by the policy will not be added to the coverage for the involved or chosen auto.

The policy cannot be transferred to anyone without Allstate's written consent, and it can be changed only by endorsement. The insured may cancel the policy by writing to Allstate with the future date on which coverage should stop; a refund, if due, will be proportional to the time the policy has been in effect, but cancellation will be effective even if the refund is not made immediately. Allstate may cancel part or all of the policy by mailing notice to the insured at their last known address. During the first 60 days the original policy is in effect, Allstate will give at least 10 days' notice of cancellation. After the first 60 days, if Allstate cancels for any reason other than non-payment of premium, it will give 30 days' notice of cancellation. After the original policy has been in effect 60 days, Allstate will not cancel the policy unless certain conditions are met, namely: the premium is not paid when due; the insured or any member of their household is convicted of a crime due to acts which increase the hazard insured against; fraud or material misrepresentation is used in obtaining the policy or making a claim; an act or omission, or a violation of any condition of the policy, occurs during the policy period which substantially and materially increases the hazard insured against; a material change in the nature or extent of the risk occurs during the policy period which causes the risk of loss to be substantially and materially increased; or Allstate has mailed notice within the first 60 days that it does not intend to continue the policy. If Allstate does not intend to continue the policy beyond the current policy period, it will mail notice at least 30 days before the end of the policy period. Changes that result in a premium adjustment include, but are not limited to, autos insured by the policy, including changes in use.

28,	"INSURED AUTO","OBJECT",**INSURED AUTO**

An "insured auto" is a motor vehicle covered under the policy. It is typically an auto described on the Policy Declarations, and liability limits apply to each insured auto. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A temporary substitute vehicle—a four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto not owned by the policyholder or a resident, temporarily used while the insured auto is serviced, repaired, stolen, or destroyed—also qualifies as an insured auto. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

69,	"INSURED AUTO","OBJECT",**INSURED AUTO**

An "insured auto" is a motor vehicle covered under the policy. It is typically an auto described on the Policy Declarations, and liability limits apply to each insured auto. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A temporary substitute vehicle—a four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto not owned by the policyholder or a resident, temporarily used while the insured auto is serviced, repaired, stolen, or destroyed—also qualifies as an insured auto. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

If Allstate does not intend to continue the policy beyond the current policy period, it will mail notice at least 30 days before the end of the policy period. Changes that result in a premium adjustment include, but are not limited to, autos insured by the policy, including changes in use.

58,	"INSURED AUTO","OBJECT",**INSURED AUTO**

An "insured auto" is a motor vehicle covered under the policy. It is typically an auto described on the Policy Declarations, and liability limits apply to each insured auto. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A temporary substitute vehicle—a four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto not owned by the policyholder or a resident, temporarily used while the insured auto is serviced, repaired, stolen, or destroyed—also qualifies as an insured auto. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

68,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

23,	"INSURED AUTO","OBJECT",**INSURED AUTO**

An "insured auto" is a motor vehicle covered under the policy. It is typically an auto described on the Policy Declarations, and liability limits apply to each insured auto. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A temporary substitute vehicle—a four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto not owned by the policyholder or a resident, temporarily used while the insured auto is serviced, repaired, stolen, or destroyed—also qualifies as an insured auto. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

## Payment Of Benefits; Autopsy

The benefit is payable to the deceased insured person's spouse. The spouse must be a resident of the same household as the insured person at the time of the accident. However, if the deceased is a minor, the benefit is payable to either parent. That parent must be a resident of the same household as the minor at the time of the accident. In all other cases, the benefit is payable to the deceased insured person's estate.

Allstate has the right and must be given the opportunity to make an autopsy where it is not prohibited by law.

## Consent Of Beneficiary

The beneficiary's consent is not required for cancellation, assignment, change of beneficiary, or any other change under this coverage.

## Proof Of Claim; Medical Reports

As soon as possible, we must be given written proof of claim. It must include all details we may need to determine if benefits are payable.

We must be given authorization to obtain medical reports and copies of records pertinent to the claim.

## Part 4 Automobile Disability Income Protection Coverage CW

Allstate will pay the weekly benefit shown on the Policy Declarations if an insured person sustains continuous total disability as a direct result of bodily injury, sickness or disease caused by an auto accident. Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

28,	"INSURED PERSON","PERSON",**INSURED PERSON**

An insured person is a person covered under an insurance policy, and the term encompasses several categories of individuals depending on the context of the policy. Generally, an insured person includes the person or persons shown as insured on the Policy Declarations (including under Coverage CW), relatives residing in the insured's household, and any other person in, on, getting into, or getting out of an insured auto with permission. Any other person or organization liable for the use of an insured auto is also considered an insured person if the use is by an insured person as described above. Additionally, the spouse of an insured person must be a resident of the same household at the time of an accident to qualify under that status.

An insured person is protected from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance, or use, including loading or unloading, of an insured auto. The insured person may be legally obligated to pay damages because of bodily injury and property damage, including bodily injury sustained by any person and damage to or destruction of property. An insured person may also be someone who incurs reasonable expenses for necessary medical treatment, services, or products, or who sustains continuous total disability as a direct result of bodily injury, sickness, or disease caused by an auto accident. An insured person may die as the result of a covered auto accident, and benefits are paid only while the insured person is alive. The insured person is the person to whom any amount due is payable.

Allstate defends an insured person when sued for damages covered by the policy, even if the suit is groundless or false. However, an insured person sued for damages not covered by the policy will not be defended by Allstate. The insured person may be asked to attend hearings or trials to defend against a bodily injury suit and may receive up to $50 per day for loss of wages or salary. The insured person must be informed immediately if sued as the result of an auto accident. The insured person must cooperate with the insurer in the investigation, settlement, and defense of any claim or lawsuit, and must help obtain payment from anyone jointly responsible. If an insured person sues a person believed responsible for the accident without giving the insurer notice, the insurer is not bound by any resulting judgment. The insured person may be required to take proper action to preserve all rights to recover damages. The insured person will be repaid by Allstate for interest accruing on damages awarded.

An "insured auto" is a motor vehicle covered under the policy. It is typically an auto described on the Policy Declarations, and liability limits apply to each insured auto. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A temporary substitute vehicle—a four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto not owned by the policyholder or a resident, temporarily used while the insured auto is serviced, repaired, stolen, or destroyed—also qualifies as an insured auto. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

41,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

12,	"POLICY","DOCUMENT",The entity referred to as "POLICY" constitutes a legal insurance contract between the insured individual and the insurer, Allstate, that applies only during the policy period and may apply to an accident on a primary basis. Under this policy, an insured person is protected from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto, and Allstate will defend an insured person sued for damages covered by the policy, even if the suit is groundless or false. The limits available for any other auto covered by the policy will not be added to the coverage for the involved or chosen auto.

The policy cannot be transferred to anyone without Allstate's written consent, and it can be changed only by endorsement. The insured may cancel the policy by writing to Allstate with the future date on which coverage should stop; a refund, if due, will be proportional to the time the policy has been in effect, but cancellation will be effective even if the refund is not made immediately. Allstate may cancel part or all of the policy by mailing notice to the insured at their last known address. During the first 60 days the original policy is in effect, Allstate will give at least 10 days' notice of cancellation. After the first 60 days, if Allstate cancels for any reason other than non-payment of premium, it will give 30 days' notice of cancellation. After the original policy has been in effect 60 days, Allstate will not cancel the policy unless certain conditions are met, namely: the premium is not paid when due; the insured or any member of their household is convicted of a crime due to acts which increase the hazard insured against; fraud or material misrepresentation is used in obtaining the policy or making a claim; an act or omission, or a violation of any condition of the policy, occurs during the policy period which substantially and materially increases the hazard insured against; a material change in the nature or extent of the risk occurs during the policy period which causes the risk of loss to be substantially and materially increased; or Allstate has mailed notice within the first 60 days that it does not intend to continue the policy. If Allstate does not intend to continue the policy beyond the current policy period, it will mail notice at least 30 days before the end of the policy period. Changes that result in a premium adjustment include, but are not limited to, autos insured by the policy, including changes in use.

57,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

## Part 6 Protection Against Loss To The Auto

The following coverages apply when indicated on the Policy Declarations. Additional payments, autos insured, definitions, exclusions, and other information applicable to all these coverages appear beginning on page 14.

## COVERAGE DD Auto Collision Insurance

Allstate will pay for direct and accidental loss to your insured auto or a non-owned auto (including insured loss to an attached trailer) from a collision with another object or by upset of that auto or trailer. An insured person may also be someone who incurs reasonable expenses for necessary medical treatment, services, or products, or who sustains continuous total disability as a direct result of bodily injury, sickness, or disease caused by an auto accident. 31,	"INSURED AUTO","OBJECT",**INSURED AUTO**

An "insured auto" is a motor vehicle covered under the policy. It is typically an auto described on the Policy Declarations, and liability limits apply to each insured auto. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A temporary substitute vehicle—a four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto not owned by the policyholder or a resident, temporarily used while the insured auto is serviced, repaired, stolen, or destroyed—also qualifies as an insured auto. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

## Part 2 Automobile Medical Payments Coverage CC

Allstate will pay to or on behalf of an insured person all reasonable expenses actually incurred by an insured person for necessary medical treatment, services, or products actually provided to the insured person. Payments will be made only when bodily injury, sickness, disease, or death is caused by an auto accident. Ambulance, hospital, medical, surgical, X-ray, dental, orthopedic and prosthetic devices, professional nursing services, pharmaceuticals, eyeglasses, hearing aids, and funeral service expenses are covered.

The treatment, services, or products must be rendered within one year after the accident. This will be extended to five years if the amount of insurance shown on the Policy Declarations for this coverage is more than $5,000.

This coverage does not apply to any person to the extent that the treatment is covered under any workers compensation law.

## Insured Persons

1. You and any resident relative who sustains bodily injury while in, on, getting into or out of, or when struck by, an auto or trailer. The use of a non-owned auto must be with the owner's permission.
2. Any other person who sustains bodily injury while in, on, getting into or out of
- a) your insured auto while being used by you, a resident relative, or any other person with your permission.
- b) a non-owned auto if the injury results from your operation or occupancy.
- c) a non-owned auto if the injury results from the operation on your behalf by your private chauffeur or domestic servant.
- d) a non-owned private passenger auto or trailer if the injury results from the operation or occupancy by a resident relative.

The use of non-owned autos must be with the owner's permission.

## Insured Autos

- D 1. Any auto described on the Policy Declarations. This includes the four wheel private passenger auto or utility auto you replace it with.
- U 3. A substitute four wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, not owned by you or a resident, temporarily used while your insured auto is being serviced or repaired, or if your insured auto is stolen or destroyed.
- O C 2. An additional four wheel private passenger auto or utility auto you become the owner of during the policy period. This auto will be covered if we insure all other private passenger autos or utility autos you own. You must, however, tell us within 60 days of acquiring the auto . You must pay any additional premium.
- M 4. A non-owned auto having not less than four wheels used with the owner's permission. This auto must not be available or furnished for the regular use of an insured person.

19,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

84,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

54,	"INSURED AUTO","OBJECT",**INSURED AUTO**

An "insured auto" is a motor vehicle covered under the policy. It is typically an auto described on the Policy Declarations, and liability limits apply to each insured auto. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A temporary substitute vehicle—a four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto not owned by the policyholder or a resident, temporarily used while the insured auto is serviced, repaired, stolen, or destroyed—also qualifies as an insured auto. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

50,	"INSURED AUTO","OBJECT",**INSURED AUTO**

An "insured auto" is a motor vehicle covered under the policy. It is typically an auto described on the Policy Declarations, and liability limits apply to each insured auto. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A temporary substitute vehicle—a four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto not owned by the policyholder or a resident, temporarily used while the insured auto is serviced, repaired, stolen, or destroyed—also qualifies as an insured auto. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

14,	"INSURED PERSON","PERSON",**INSURED PERSON**

An insured person is a person covered under an insurance policy, and the term encompasses several categories of individuals depending on the context of the policy. Generally, an insured person includes the person or persons shown as insured on the Policy Declarations (including under Coverage CW), relatives residing in the insured's household, and any other person in, on, getting into, or getting out of an insured auto with permission. Any other person or organization liable for the use of an insured auto is also considered an insured person if the use is by an insured person as described above. Additionally, the spouse of an insured person must be a resident of the same household at the time of an accident to qualify under that status.

An insured person is protected from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance, or use, including loading or unloading, of an insured auto. The insured person may be legally obligated to pay damages because of bodily injury and property damage, including bodily injury sustained by any person and damage to or destruction of property. An insured person may also be someone who incurs reasonable expenses for necessary medical treatment, services, or products, or who sustains continuous total disability as a direct result of bodily injury, sickness, or disease caused by an auto accident. An insured person may die as the result of a covered auto accident, and benefits are paid only while the insured person is alive. The insured person is the person to whom any amount due is payable.

Allstate defends an insured person when sued for damages covered by the policy, even if the suit is groundless or false. However, an insured person sued for damages not covered by the policy will not be defended by Allstate. The insured person may be asked to attend hearings or trials to defend against a bodily injury suit and may receive up to $50 per day for loss of wages or salary. The insured person must be informed immediately if sued as the result of an auto accident. The insured person must cooperate with the insurer in the investigation, settlement, and defense of any claim or lawsuit, and must help obtain payment from anyone jointly responsible. If an insured person sues a person believed responsible for the accident without giving the insurer notice, the insurer is not bound by any resulting judgment. The insured person may be required to take proper action to preserve all rights to recover damages. The insured person will be repaid by Allstate for interest accruing on damages awarded.

28,	"INSURED AUTO","OBJECT",**INSURED AUTO**

An "insured auto" is a motor vehicle covered under the policy. It is typically an auto described on the Policy Declarations, and liability limits apply to each insured auto. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A temporary substitute vehicle—a four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto not owned by the policyholder or a resident, temporarily used while the insured auto is serviced, repaired, stolen, or destroyed—also qualifies as an insured auto. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

31,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.
