1,	LIMITS OF LIABILITY

THE LIMIT SHOWN ON THE POLICY DECLARATIONS IS THE MAXIMUM WE WILL PAY FOR ALL EXPENSES INCURRED BY OR FOR EACH INSURED PERSON AS THE RESULT OF ANY ONE AUTO ACCIDENT.

THE MEDICAL PAYMENTS LIMIT APPLIES TO EACH INSURED AUTO AS STATED ON THE POLICY DECLARATIONS. THE INSURING OF MORE THAN ONE PERSON OR AUTO UNDER THIS POLICY WILL NOT INCREASE OUR LIMIT BEYOND THE AMOUNT SHOWNFOR ANY ONE AUTO , EVEN THOUGH A SEPARATE PREMIUM IS CHARGED FOR EACH AUTO . THE LIMIT ALSO WILL NOT BE INCREASED IF YOU HAVE OTHER AUTO INSURANCE POLICIES THAT APPLY.

D If an insured person dies as the result of a covered auto accident, we will pay the least of the following as a funeral service expenses benefit:

1. $2,000; or
2. O 2. the Coverage CC limit of liability stated on the Policy Declarations; or
3. C 3. the remaining portion of the Coverage CC limit of liability not expended for other covered medical expenses.

U M E This funeral service expenses benefit does not increase, and will not be paid in addition to, the limits of liability stated on the Policy Declarations for Coverage CC. This benefit is payable to the deceased insured person's spouse if a resident of the same household at the time of the accident. However, if the deceased is a minor, the benefit is payable to either parent if that parent is a resident of the same household at the time of the accident. In all other cases, the benefit is payable to the deceased insured person's estate.

## Allstate Insurance Company

S A THERE WILL BE NO DUPLICATION OF PAYMENTS MADE UNDER THE BODILY INJURY LIABILITY AND AUTOMOBILE MEDICAL PAYMENTS COVERAGES OF THIS POLICY. ALL PAYMENTS MADE TO OR ON BEHALF OF ANY PERSON UNDER THIS COVERAGE WILL BE CONSIDERED AS ADVANCE PAYMENTS TO THAT PERSON. THE DAMAGES PAYABLE UNDER THE BODILY INJURY LIABILITY COVERAGE OF THIS POLICY WILL BE REDUCED BY THAT AMOUNT.

## M Unreasonable Or Unnecessary Medical Expenses

P L E If the insured person incurs medical expenses which are unreasonable or unnecessary, we may refuse to pay for those expenses and contest them. Unreasonable medical expenses are fees for medical services which are substantially higher than the usual and customary charges for those services. Unnecessary medical expenses are fees for medical services which are not usually and customarily performed for treatment of the injury, including fees for an excessive number, amount, or duration of medical services.

If the insured person is sued by a medical services provider because we refuse to pay contested medical expenses, we will pay all defense costs and any resulting judgment against the insured person. We will choose the counsel. The insured person must cooperate with us in the defense of any claim or lawsuit. If we ask the insured person to attend hearings or trials, we will pay up to $50 per day for loss of wages or salary. We will also pay other reasonable expenses incurred at our request.

## IF THERE IS OTHER INSURANCE

WHEN THIS COVERAGE APPLIES TO A SUBSTITUTE AUTO OR NON-OWNED AUTO, ALLSTATE WILL PAY ONLY AFTER ALL OTHER COLLECTIBLE AUTO MEDICAL INSURANCE HAS BEEN EXHAUSTED.

WHEN THIS COVERAGE APPLIES TO A REPLACEMENT AUTO OR ADDITIONAL AUTO , THIS POLICY WILL NOT APPLY IF YOU HAVE OTHER COLLECTIBLE AUTO MEDICAL INSURANCE.

## Assistance And Cooperation

When we ask, an insured person must cooperate with us in the investigation, settlement and defense of any claim or lawsuit. If we ask, that person must also help us obtain payment from anyone who may be jointly responsible.

We can't be obligated if an insured person voluntarily takes any action or makes any payments other than for covered expenses for first aid to others.

## Action Against Allstate

No one may sue us under this coverage unless there is full compliance with all the policy terms.

## Proof Of Claim; Medical Reports

As soon as possible, any person making claim must give us written proof of claim. It must include all details we may need to determine the amounts payable. We may also require any person making claim to submit to questioning under oath and sign the transcript.

The injured person may be required to take medical examinations by physicians we choose, as often as we reasonably require. We must be given authorization to obtain medical reports and other records pertinent to the claim.

## D Part 3 Automobile Death Indemnity Insurance Coverage CM

O C Allstate will pay the benefit shown on the Policy Declarations if an insured person dies as a direct result of bodily injury , sickness or disease caused by an auto accident. The injury must be sustained while the insured person is in, on, getting into or out of, or when struck as a pedestrian by an auto, trailer or semi-trailer.

Thought: Under Coverage CM, benefits are paid only if either death occurs within 90 days of the auto accident, or death occurs within 1 year and the bodily injury has continuously prevented the insured person from performing all duties pertaining to that person's occupation. A death 6 months (about 180 days) after the accident falls outside the 90-day window, so the only applicable condition is the 1-year provision requiring continuous prevention from performing occupational duties.

Answer: The bodily injury must have continuously prevented the insured person from performing all duties pertaining to that person's occupation.
per_question.answer: The bodily injury must have continuously prevented the insured person from performing all duties pertaining to that person's occupation.
per_question.judge_response:
The LLM answer captures the core condition from the correct answer: the injury must have continuously prevented the person from performing their occupation. The added detail "all duties pertaining to that person's occupation" is consistent with and clarifies the same requirement, not a contradiction. Therefore, it is fully correct.

A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. ## Part 2 Automobile Medical Payments Coverage CC

Allstate will pay to or on behalf of an insured person all reasonable expenses actually incurred by an insured person for necessary medical treatment, services, or products actually provided to the insured person. Payments will be made only when bodily injury, sickness, disease, or death is caused by an auto accident. Ambulance, hospital, medical, surgical, X-ray, dental, orthopedic and prosthetic devices, professional nursing services, pharmaceuticals, eyeglasses, hearing aids, and funeral service expenses are covered.

The treatment, services, or products must be rendered within one year after the accident. This will be extended to five years if the amount of insurance shown on the Policy Declarations for this coverage is more than $5,000.

This coverage does not apply to any person to the extent that the treatment is covered under any workers compensation law.

## Insured Persons

1. You and any resident relative who sustains bodily injury while in, on, getting into or out of, or when struck by, an auto or trailer. The use of a non-owned auto must be with the owner's permission.
2. Any other person who sustains bodily injury while in, on, getting into or out of
- a) your insured auto while being used by you, a resident relative, or any other person with your permission.
- b) a non-owned auto if the injury results from your operation or occupancy.
- c) a non-owned auto if the injury results from the operation on your behalf by your private chauffeur or domestic servant.
- d) a non-owned private passenger auto or trailer if the injury results from the operation or occupancy by a resident relative.

The use of non-owned autos must be with the owner's permission.

## Insured Autos

- D 1. Any auto described on the Policy Declarations. This includes the four wheel private passenger auto or utility auto you replace it with.
- U 3. A substitute four wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, not owned by you or a resident, temporarily used while your insured auto is being serviced or repaired, or if your insured auto is stolen or destroyed.
- O C 2. An additional four wheel private passenger auto or utility auto you become the owner of during the policy period. This auto will be covered if we insure all other private passenger autos or utility autos you own. You must, however, tell us within 60 days of acquiring the auto . You must pay any additional premium.
- M 4. A non-owned auto having not less than four wheels used with the owner's permission. This auto must not be available or furnished for the regular use of an insured person.
- E 5. A trailer while attached to an insured auto . The trailer must be designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto. This trailer can't

## Allstate Insurance Company

be used for business purposes with other than a private passenger auto or utility auto .

- A 1. "Allstate", "We", "Us", or "Our" \_\_ means the Allstate Insurance Company or Allstate Indemnity Company as shown on the Policy Declarations.

## S Definitions

- M 2. "Auto" \_\_ means a land motor vehicle designed for use on public roads.
- L E 4. "Utility Auto" \_\_ means an auto of the pickup body, sedan delivery or panel truck type. This auto must have a rated load capacity of not more than 2,000 pounds.
- P 3. "Resident" \_\_ means a person who physically resides in your household with the intention of continuing residence there. Your unmarried dependent children while temporarily away from home will be considered residents if they intend to resume residing in your household.
5. "You" or "Your" \_\_ means the policyholder named on the Policy Declarations and that policyholder's resident spouse.

## Exclusions \_\_ What is not covered

This coverage does not apply to bodily injury, sickness, disease or death to

1. you or a resident relative while in, on, getting into or out of an auto you or a resident relative own but do not insure for this coverage.
2. you or a resident relative while in, on, getting into or out of, or struck as a pedestrian by:
- a) a vehicle operated on rails or crawler-treads, or
- b) a vehicle or other equipment designed for use off public roads, while not on public roads.
3. any person while in, on, getting into or out of:
- a) an owned auto while available for hire to the public. This exclusion does not apply to shared-expense car pools.
- b) an auto or trailer while used as a residence or premises.
4. any person, other than you or a resident relative, while using a non-owned auto:
- a) which is available for hire by the public, or
- b) in auto business operations such as repairing, servicing, testing, washing, parking, storing or selling of autos .

Coverage is provided for you, your private chauffeur or domestic servant while using a private passenger auto or trailer in any other business or occupation.

18,	"INSURED AUTO","OBJECT",**INSURED AUTO**

An "insured auto" is a motor vehicle covered under the policy. It is typically an auto described on the Policy Declarations, and liability limits apply to each insured auto. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A temporary substitute vehicle—a four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto not owned by the policyholder or a resident, temporarily used while the insured auto is serviced, repaired, stolen, or destroyed—also qualifies as an insured auto. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

## Payment Of Benefits; Autopsy

The benefit is payable to the deceased insured person's spouse. The spouse must be a resident of the same household as the insured person at the time of the accident. Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

14,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

Ambulance, hospital, medical, surgical, X-ray, dental, orthopedic and prosthetic devices, professional nursing services, pharmaceuticals, eyeglasses, hearing aids, and funeral service expenses are covered.

The treatment, services, or products must be rendered within one year after the accident. This will be extended to five years if the amount of insurance shown on the Policy Declarations for this coverage is more than $5,000.

This coverage does not apply to any person to the extent that the treatment is covered under any workers compensation law.

P L E If the insured person incurs medical expenses which are unreasonable or unnecessary, we may refuse to pay for those expenses and contest them. 11,	"INSURED AUTO","OBJECT",**INSURED AUTO**

An "insured auto" is a motor vehicle covered under the policy. It is typically an auto described on the Policy Declarations, and liability limits apply to each insured auto. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A temporary substitute vehicle—a four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto not owned by the policyholder or a resident, temporarily used while the insured auto is serviced, repaired, stolen, or destroyed—also qualifies as an insured auto. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

You must protect these rights and help us enforce them." This indicates that when Allstate pays a loss, the insured's rights of recovery from the at-fault party transfer to Allstate, up to the amount Allstate paid. The question asks what happens to money Allstate later recovers from the person at fault. Under subrogation, the recovered money belongs to Allstate up to the amount it paid. The context does not explicitly state what happens to any excess, but it does establish that Allstate's rights of recovery become theirs up to the amount paid. Therefore, the money recovered goes to Allstate up to what it paid out.

Answer: When Allstate pays a loss, the insured's rights of recovery from anyone else become Allstate's up to the amount Allstate has paid. So any money Allstate later recovers from the person at fault belongs to Allstate up to the amount it paid.

Generally, an insured person includes the person or persons shown as insured on the Policy Declarations (including under Coverage CW), relatives residing in the insured's household, and any other person in, on, getting into, or getting out of an insured auto with permission. Any other person or organization liable for the use of an insured auto is also considered an insured person if the use is by an insured person as described above. Additionally, the spouse of an insured person must be a resident of the same household at the time of an accident to qualify under that status.

An insured person is protected from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance, or use, including loading or unloading, of an insured auto. The insured person may be legally obligated to pay damages because of bodily injury and property damage, including bodily injury sustained by any person and damage to or destruction of property. An insured person may also be someone who incurs reasonable expenses for necessary medical treatment, services, or products, or who sustains continuous total disability as a direct result of bodily injury, sickness, or disease caused by an auto accident. Allstate defends an insured person when sued for damages covered by the policy, even if the suit is groundless or false. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. 45,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

Additionally, the spouse of an insured person must be a resident of the same household at the time of an accident to qualify under that status.

An insured person is protected from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance, or use, including loading or unloading, of an insured auto. The insured person may be legally obligated to pay damages because of bodily injury and property damage, including bodily injury sustained by any person and damage to or destruction of property. An insured person may also be someone who incurs reasonable expenses for necessary medical treatment, services, or products, or who sustains continuous total disability as a direct result of bodily injury, sickness, or disease caused by an auto accident. An insured person may die as the result of a covered auto accident, and benefits are paid only while the insured person is alive. The insured person is the person to whom any amount due is payable.

Allstate defends an insured person when sued for damages covered by the policy, even if the suit is groundless or false. However, an insured person sued for damages not covered by the policy will not be defended by Allstate. The insured person may be asked to attend hearings or trials to defend against a bodily injury suit and may receive up to $50 per day for loss of wages or salary. The insured person must be informed immediately if sued as the result of an auto accident. The insured person must cooperate with the insurer in the investigation, settlement, and defense of any claim or lawsuit, and must help obtain payment from anyone jointly responsible. If an insured person sues a person believed responsible for the accident without giving the insurer notice, the insurer is not bound by any resulting judgment. The insured person may be required to take proper action to preserve all rights to recover damages. The insured person will be repaid by Allstate for interest accruing on damages awarded.

An "insured auto" is a motor vehicle covered under the policy. It is typically an auto described on the Policy Declarations, and liability limits apply to each insured auto. The term also encompasses a replacement four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto, as well as an additional four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period, provided all other private passenger autos or utility autos owned are insured. A temporary substitute vehicle—a four-wheel private passenger auto or utility auto not owned by the policyholder or a resident, temporarily used while the insured auto is serviced, repaired, stolen, or destroyed—also qualifies as an insured auto. A trailer designed for use with a private passenger auto or utility auto is included while attached to an insured auto.

Beyond owned and declared vehicles, an insured auto includes a non-owned vehicle operated with permission, and a non-owned vehicle not available for public hire. It also covers an auto used by a person or organization liable for its use, provided the auto is not owned or hired by that person or organization, as well as an auto used by the policyholder or any other person with the policyholder's permission. The policy protects an insured person from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use, loading or unloading of an insured auto.

The insured auto is covered under various provisions: the medical payments limit applies to it; clothing and personal luggage may be located in it; it may be transported, resulting in general average and salvage charges; it is covered under Coverage DD for collision losses and under comprehensive insurance; it may contain devices constituting a sound system; and it may be involved in situations requiring bail bonds following an accident or traffic law violation, or in an auto accident where first aid expenses are incurred. When used to carry persons or property for a charge, the insured auto remains subject to the terms of the policy.

76,	"POLICY DECLARATIONS","DOCUMENT",**POLICY DECLARATIONS**

Policy Declarations is a document that forms part of the legal contract between the insured and Allstate, showing the premiums for each coverage and each insured auto. It describes the autos covered under the policy, identifying any auto covered as an insured auto, and indicates which coverages apply. The Policy Declarations names the policyholder, shows which Allstate company is designated as "Us" or is the insurer, and shows the person or persons insured under Coverage CW. It also shows the policy period and the address where stolen property may be returned.

Regarding liability, the Policy Declarations is a document showing the limit of Allstate's liability—the maximum amount the insurer will pay for all expenses incurred by or for each insured person as the result of any one auto accident—as well as the total limit of Allstate's liability for each loss, including the total limit of liability for each loss under Coverage JJ. If an insured has two or more autos insured in their name and one of these autos is involved in an accident, only the coverage limits shown on the Policy Declarations for that auto will apply. If none of the insured autos is involved in the accident, the insured may choose any single auto shown on the Policy Declarations and the coverage limits applicable to that auto will apply. However, vehicles or persons shown on the Policy Declarations do not affect the maximum limits Allstate will pay.

The Policy Declarations also shows the amount of insurance for each coverage, the coverage limits and the vehicles or persons covered, the deductible for each coverage, and the medical payments limit applicable to each insured auto. A coverage applies only when a premium for it is shown on the Policy Declarations. A specific premium for a rented vehicle must be shown on the Policy Declarations to remove the exclusion. A covered trailer not described on the Policy Declarations has a loss limit of $500. The camper unit exclusion does not apply if the camper unit is described on the Policy Declarations, and the camper unit may be described on the Policy Declarations. Finally, the Policy Declarations is the document on which the policy must be countersigned by an authorized agent if required by state law.

The limits available for any other auto covered by the policy will not be added to the coverage for the involved or chosen auto.

The policy cannot be transferred to anyone without Allstate's written consent, and it can be changed only by endorsement. The insured may cancel the policy by writing to Allstate with the future date on which coverage should stop; a refund, if due, will be proportional to the time the policy has been in effect, but cancellation will be effective even if the refund is not made immediately. Allstate may cancel part or all of the policy by mailing notice to the insured at their last known address. During the first 60 days the original policy is in effect, Allstate will give at least 10 days' notice of cancellation. After the first 60 days, if Allstate cancels for any reason other than non-payment of premium, it will give 30 days' notice of cancellation. After the original policy has been in effect 60 days, Allstate will not cancel the policy unless certain conditions are met, namely: the premium is not paid when due; the insured or any member of their household is convicted of a crime due to acts which increase the hazard insured against; fraud or material misrepresentation is used in obtaining the policy or making a claim; an act or omission, or a violation of any condition of the policy, occurs during the policy period which substantially and materially increases the hazard insured against; a material change in the nature or extent of the risk occurs during the policy period which causes the risk of loss to be substantially and materially increased; or Allstate has mailed notice within the first 60 days that it does not intend to continue the policy. If Allstate does not intend to continue the policy beyond the current policy period, it will mail notice at least 30 days before the end of the policy period. Changes that result in a premium adjustment include, but are not limited to, autos insured by the policy, including changes in use.

10,	"INSURED PERSON","PERSON",**INSURED PERSON**

An insured person is a person covered under an insurance policy, and the term encompasses several categories of individuals depending on the context of the policy. Generally, an insured person includes the person or persons shown as insured on the Policy Declarations (including under Coverage CW), relatives residing in the insured's household, and any other person in, on, getting into, or getting out of an insured auto with permission. Any other person or organization liable for the use of an insured auto is also considered an insured person if the use is by an insured person as described above. Additionally, the spouse of an insured person must be a resident of the same household at the time of an accident to qualify under that status.

An insured person is protected from liability for damages arising out of the ownership, maintenance, or use, including loading or unloading, of an insured auto. The insured person may be legally obligated to pay damages because of bodily injury and property damage, including bodily injury sustained by any person and damage to or destruction of property. An insured person may also be someone who incurs reasonable expenses for necessary medical treatment, services, or products, or who sustains continuous total disability as a direct result of bodily injury, sickness, or disease caused by an auto accident. An insured person may die as the result of a covered auto accident, and benefits are paid only while the insured person is alive. The insured person is the person to whom any amount due is payable.

Allstate defends an insured person when sued for damages covered by the policy, even if the suit is groundless or false. However, an insured person sued for damages not covered by the policy will not be defended by Allstate. The insured person may be asked to attend hearings or trials to defend against a bodily injury suit and may receive up to $50 per day for loss of wages or salary. The insured person must be informed immediately if sued as the result of an auto accident. The insured person must cooperate with the insurer in the investigation, settlement, and defense of any claim or lawsuit, and must help obtain payment from anyone jointly responsible. If an insured person sues a person believed responsible for the accident without giving the insurer notice, the insurer is not bound by any resulting judgment. The insured person may be required to take proper action to preserve all rights to recover damages. The insured person will be repaid by Allstate for interest accruing on damages awarded.
